limits: This is independent source review and exact local patch replay only; no kernel or VM execution, race stress, runtime qualification or production claim.

The complete-tree occurrence audit is the owner-provided fixed-tree audit; this review independently reread and hashed six relevant original source files, and reviewed the other recorded allocation and release occurrences.
Changing fs_struct layout requires an appropriately complete rebuilt kernel before boot. Compiling only selected objects does not qualify a mixed old/new kernel.
New independent observers retain fs allocation and root/pwd paths; this intentionally does not preserve mount graph immutability or prove actual private loop issuance.
review_scope: Original users task-sharing and existing grant slots remain the only inputs to exec/CLONE_FS/unshare/setns sharing predicates. The new refs value never substitutes for users.
The initial unpublished copy and init_fs each acquire exactly one aggregate refs owner. All unchanged original last-users or unpublished-copy frees now drop that one aggregate owner.
Observer acquisition remains under task_lock then fs sequence lock while an attached task owns a positive users slot. Actor destruction drops an independent ref outside spinlocks.

Last task exit, failed clone cleanup, both unshare paths, temporary nsset copy destruction and the original grant consume/expiry retain the original users transitions. The aggregate remains alive if its original grant users slot survives a task detachment.
Final refcount release alone releases the held fs paths and allocation; observer references prevent allocation ABA without granting execution or device authority.
Original grant kernel/p4_guest_mntns.c fresh whole-body hash is unchanged and absent from the exact four-path patch.
Exec remains a bounded identity observation: in_exec or later mm/cred/task/fs differences reject. There is no new live lease, graph proof, issuer, device operation or block access path.
